metadata.title: Show a solution, ban it, see what replaces it (exposure-ban experiment, Qwen3-8B bf16)
metadata.method: exposure bans (NAMED / UNNAMED) scored against four committed forecast families: SUBTRACT-IN-CONTEXT (iterated persistent signature veto under the copy-twin prompt), LADDER (default), ASSOCIATE (frozen 'standard alternative to Y'), PROXIMITY (Zhang-Shasha nearest survivor)
metadata.baselines: COPY twin (same prefix, no prohibition), UNNAMED generic 'different algorithm', the ban-free signature veto counterfactual and the context-free default (bf16 baseline check)
deviations: Seeds: plan 0.12 writes seed = sha256(sample_id) with the arm inside sample_id, while 2.2/T2 require seed indices shared across arms so that each veto sample matches its COPY twin up to the first vetoed position. Implemented common random numbers: seed = int(sha256('task:Y:p{i}:s{j}')[:8], 16), identical in COPY, every veto round, NAMED, UNNAMED and W1-W4; sample_id still carries arm and round.

T1(f): the plan expects the frozen counting rule (>= 0.10 nats on >= 3 events) to advance nothing in >= 95% of null draws. Measured on 200 simulated null draws of 15 events (random point-mass forecasts, landing independent of forecasts): some family advances in 85% of draws, while the Holm-corrected Wilcoxon tests flag a difference in 2% (planted winner advances in 98%). The rule was kept as frozen; the test asserts the Holm-Wilcoxon level instead, and the C1 verdict is reported next to a label-permutation placebo on the real events.

Caches: HF_HOME / HF_HUB_CACHE point at the run's shared cache (the environment forbids overriding them), so the plan's ./hf_cache does not exist; vLLM / Triton / XDG caches live under ./.cache/ instead of ./vllm_cache/.

Hardware: one NVIDIA L4 (23 GB), not the A4500 (20 GB) the plan assumed. No C compiler exists on the machine, so Triton / torch.compile cannot build kernels: vLLM runs with enforce_eager=True and TORCH_COMPILE_DISABLE=1 from the start (as exp11 did), bf16 weights as planned.

Environment: the venv reuses exp11's 160 pinned packages (vllm 0.11.0, torch 2.8.0, transformers 4.57.1, scipy 1.18.1) plus zss 1.2.0, pytest, matplotlib and pandas, so the bench modules run on the versions they were frozen with.
Judge: the bench Judge class is used unchanged except its module-level PERSONAL_CAP, set to USD 0.50 (the plan's stop line) instead of exp11's 1.40.

Prompts: the W1-W4 template-arm prompts (frozen wordings found in the round-2 experiment-12 prompts_v2.json: W1 'Do not use {X} for this task.', W2 'Your solution must not rely on {X}.', W3 'Avoid {X} entirely.', W4 '{X} is not allowed here.') were rendered and committed in COMMIT #1 together with COPY / NAMED / UNNAMED, so the optional arm samples only committed prompts.

Shown-program pools: deduplication by canon_tokens hash is very aggressive on Qwen's near-identical forced programs (e.g. T10 bfs 40 -> 1, T06 sort_adjacent 21 -> 1, T04 builtin 24 -> 1), so 11 of 33 Y show a single program and program-level heterogeneity cannot be estimated for them (flagged n_shown_lt5).
Proximity: all 2,972 Zhang-Shasha pairs were computed with up to 20 references per survivor (projection about 12 min on 6 processes, under the 30-min cap), so no cap was applied.

Implementation bug found and fixed during stage 1: the round r+1 n-gram was first selected on vLLM output token_ids, which keep the stop token <|im_end|>; it has presence 1.0 and collateral 0, so it was chosen for T03 size_k_heap and vetoing it stopped the model from ending (1,024-token rambles). The 750 round-2 samples drawn with these masks were discarded (kept for the record in data/discarded_round2_stop_token_bug.jsonl, log logs/stage1_attempt1_stop_token_bug.out) and round 2 was redrawn with the corrected rule: canonical tokenisation of fenced(extracted code) of the round-r Y-labelled programs, exactly as for g*. Round 1 (g* from canonical tokenisation) was unaffected and kept.
